title: Understanding Bluff and Fold in Texas Hold'em
summaryJa: ポーカーの「ブラフ」は弱い手でも強いふりをして相手を騙すテクニックで、「フォールド」は手を降りることです。この2つは基本的だが重要な戦略です。
segments: Texas Hold'em has two important words that all players should know: bluff and fold. These words describe key actions in the game.
Understanding them helps you play better poker. A bluff is when you bet money even though your cards are not very good.
You want to make other players think your cards are strong. For example, you have only a low pair.
But you bet a lot of money. Other players see your big bet and think you have better cards.
They get scared and do not want to lose money. Many of them fold their cards.
Then you win the hand. Fold means to stop playing your current hand and give up.
When you fold, you leave the game and lose any money you already put in the pot. For example, another player bets a lot of money.
You look at your cards and see they are weak. You do not want to lose more money.
So you fold. Now you are out of that hand.
A good player folds often. Folding saves your money for better hands later.
Bluff and fold work together in poker. Smart players bluff sometimes.
But they also fold when the risk is too high. New players often make mistakes.
They bluff too much or fold too much. The best players balance both actions.
They know when to be brave and when to be careful. This is what makes Texas Hold'em fun and exciting.
